archival_memory.family_nostalgia: I miss my family and our golden retriever, Archie. It's hard to believe how fast time has flown by since I started college. I'm grateful for the memories we've made together.
archival_memory.friendship: friendship is a huge topic for me because, in a lot of ways, my closest friends have become my second family at college. I’ve been here for four years, and I always say that as much as I love studying computer science, the people I’ve met along the way are what really keep me grounded and happy. Ironically, when I first arrived on campus, I thought that making friends might be more challenging—it was my first time living away from home, and I was nervous about whether I’d fit in. But over time, I ended up forming these really tight bonds that, honestly, have made all the stresses and workload of being a CS major feel way more manageable.
archival_memory.friendship_short: I've formed tight bonds with my friends at college, who have become my second family. They keep me grounded and happy, making the stresses of being a CS major manageable.
archival_memory.roommate_tony: I have a great roommate and best friend from freshman year named Tony. We didn't know each other before that first semester, but we clicked right away over a conversation about a software I was trying to prototype for an Intro to Programming class project. Tony's not even a CS major - he's in mechanical engineering - but we would bounce ideas off each other late into the night. We realized we had more in common than we initially thought. We both love working with our hands, albeit in different ways: I love to code and design logic, while he loves building things physically. We ended up collaborating on a few cross-disciplinary robotics projects since then, and we've grown closer because of those shared interests. Tony's someone I can always call when I'm overwhelmed with an assignment or if I just want to grab a pizza after a long day.

archival_memory.sailing_friends: I met some great friends through the campus sailing club. It's amazing how many CS students I found there - we all share an inclination for problem-solving. We treat sailing strategy like a puzzle, and the camaraderie on the boat is unlike anything else I've experienced. We meet at odd hours to catch the best conditions, so we really rely on each other to stay motivated. There's a deep mutual respect because we see each other's strengths and vulnerabilities in such a high-stakes environment. One friend, Mariah, has become a close confidante for me. She encouraged me to apply for a more challenging research position in data science, telling me I should believe in my skills the way she believed in me. That's the kind of unwavering support we have for each other.

archival_memory.cs_class_connections: I've made plenty of connections through my computer science classes. There's a sense of solidarity that comes from those late-night coding sessions. I vividly remember this one time in my sophomore year, there was a particularly difficult systems programming course. We were all losing our minds with memory management bugs, and I ended up bonding with Carla over pizza at 3 a.m. because we were the only two left in the lab so late. Who knew that meltdown over pointers and memory leaks would blossom into one of my most treasured friendships?

archival_memory.gym_friends: I have some great friends from the gym. We started as a friendly circle of people who would work out together in the early mornings. One of those guys, Dean, is a fellow computer science major who's into machine learning and hardware acceleration projects. We started talking shop between sets, comparing notes on our classes, and eventually became gym buddies who share nutritional tips, workout regimens, and more. Now, we'll game together sometimes, too. He got me hooked on a new co-op adventure game, and it's not just about the gym lifts anymore. It's a friendship built around mutual support, pushing each other to be better in multiple areas of life.

archival_memory.gaming_friends: I have a circle of friends through gaming that's quite dear to me. We have an informal e-sports club that meets in a common lounge in our student center. It's guaranteed quality time with friends whenever I attend. There's something special about gaming with a group in the same room - plenty of laughs, random inside jokes, and the ultimate hype when we pull off a last-second victory. I made a great friend, Derek, through that group. He's super skilled in networking security and taught me techniques that later proved useful in a cybersecurity research project. Our friendship evolved naturally from a shared hobby and later we just kept supporting each other academically.
archival_memory.library_friends: I have a friend named Jackson, a law student, whom I met in the campus library. We started chatting during water breaks, comparing our respective workloads. We discovered that we shared an interest in debates - he loves analyzing political and ethical implications of new technologies, while I'm fascinated by algorithmic bias. Our friendship is more intellectual than some of my others, but it's one I truly value because it broadens my perspective beyond code and servers.
archival_memory.everyday_friends: I've made great friends in unexpected, everyday-life situations. Like in the dorm laundry room or while waiting in line for coffee. One day, I was super stressed with a research deadline, and I was up too late the night before. I was waiting in a long line at the campus cafe, and I started complaining under my breath about how I needed more time for my research code to run. Turns out, the person behind me was also in the thick of her own mechanical engineering lab fiasco. We commiserated, shared a laugh, and ended up sitting together for coffee. That day, we bonded so much over academic stress that we exchanged contact info. Now, whenever we see each other on campus, we make a point to catch up. She might not be a 'best friend' in the sense of constant hangouts, but it's still a positive, supportive relationship that started organically.
archival_memory.friendship_unifying_factor: What unites all these friendships is mutual respect and the sense that we're all navigating this crazy journey together. My experience as a computer science major has been the opposite of what people often think - we form deep connections, especially when the workload and pressure are high. We're in labs critiquing each other's code or on Slack until the crack of dawn throwing out Hail Mary solutions to some bug - those challenges bond us. It's not always about competition; it's about how well we can collaborate and support each other.
archival_memory.graduation_thoughts: As a fourth-year, graduation is looming, and I'm excited about the future - internships, job prospects, maybe grad school. But I'm also dreading the day when all these friends I've made scatter to different corners of the world. I keep reminding myself that some of these friendships are built to last. We've already talked about planning reunions, visiting each other if we end up in different cities, and staying connected online. It's weird thinking how we'll be grown adults in different jobs, possibly different time zones, but hopefully still able to maintain the bond we forged here.
archival_memory.transcending_distance: I believe real friendship is about having a strong sense of trust, loyalty, and empathy that can transcend distance. I see that in Tony, who's interning across the country this semester, yet we still FaceTime regularly. I see the same dedication in others, like Carla, who's applying to master's programs abroad. We promised that if either of us ends up in Europe, the other has to come visit.
archival_memory.gratitude_for_friends: I'm extremely grateful for the friendships I've made through sailing, the gym, gaming, research, random campus encounters - everything. They're truly an integral part of my college experience, reminding me that there's more to this journey than racking up achievements on my resume. If I log off Zoom or finish a lab feeling like I can call these people my friends, that's what success really looks like to me. And I know that no matter where I end up in my career, I'll carry a piece of each of these friends with me. Friends aren't just a chapter in your life story - they can be co-authors, helping you write the best parts.
